question: Visualize patient transitions between disease stages (I, II, III, IV) across three time points (T1, T2, T3) using a Sankey diagram. Flow width should be proportional to the number of patients making each transition.

files.eval_guideline: Sankey diagram must show patient transitions between disease stages across T1, T2, and T3 with flow widths proportional to patient counts; color scheme and node ordering may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename stage_transition_sankey.png and PNG image format. The name directly matches the requested Sankey diagram of patient transitions between disease stages across T1, T2, and T3.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires the diagram to show disease-stage transitions across T1, T2, and T3 with flow widths proportional to patient counts, while allowing different colors and node ordering. Semantic comparison evaluates these visual requirements without requiring pixel-level agreement.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show the same Sankey structure for patient transitions among stages I–IV across T1, T2, and T3, with flow widths proportional to patient counts. Corresponding node sizes and transition widths agree: stage totals are 38, 41, 29, and 12 at T1; 31, 40, 32, and 17 at T2; and 28, 36, 35, and 21 at T3. Both depict predominantly unchanged stages, some progression toward higher stages, and smaller reverse transitions. The candidate adds explicit time-point headings, a cohort size of 120, node counts, endpoint percentages, and labels for most flows, making the underlying quantities easier to interpret. A few narrow flows lack numerical labels, but remain visible. Colors, spacing, and label placement differ without changing the scientific content. No material transitions or stages are missing.
